faq: Can you work on an app another developer built?
Yes. We read the code first and tell you if anything looks risky to change. We follow your structure and naming, so your own team can keep working in it afterwards.
How do I give you access?
Add us as a collaborator in your Wix Dev Center and give us repository access. We never ask for passwords, and you can remove our access whenever the work is done.
Will my existing site owners be affected?
Not negatively. We test the update on a development site that already has the old version installed, so data and settings carry over, and we flag anything that needs a notice to owners.
Do new features need Wix review?
Updates to public apps can go through Wix's review. We follow their guidelines so changes pass smoothly, but timing and approval are decided by Wix.
desc:
Wix app feature development adds new capabilities, or fixes broken ones, in an app that already has users. Ecom Swift LLC reads your code, agrees the change in writing, builds it with the Wix CLI and tests that existing installs keep working.

## What is Wix app feature development?

Wix app feature development is the work of changing a live app: adding a dashboard page, a widget option, a data field, a webhook handler or a fix for a bug in an existing flow. It differs from a new build because there are already site owners, saved data and an App Market listing to protect. A good change adds value for new users without disturbing the ones you have.

## Why changing a live app needs care

A new feature that works on a fresh test site can still break an app that has been installed for a year. Older installs carry saved settings, records in collections and widgets already placed on pages. If a field is renamed, a required setting is added or a widget changes shape, those owners can lose data or find a blank space on their site.

That risk is why many app owners delay changes and live with known bugs. A careful process removes the fear. You can keep improving the app while owners continue to rely on it.

## How new features affect your app's results

Features are how an app earns its place. A missing option is often the reason a site owner chooses a competitor, and a long-standing bug is often the reason they leave a poor rating. Adding the option people ask for, or fixing the bug they keep reporting, can improve retention and support load.

Features also open up plan structure. A new widget setting or a data export can justify a paid tier. Whether a feature brings more installs or upgrades depends on your audience and listing, and we do not promise those outcomes.

## What a well-delivered feature includes

- A written scope that says exactly what will and will not change.
- Code added to your own repository, following the structure already there.
- New data fields that do not disturb existing records.
- Dashboard pages built with the Wix Design System so they match the rest of the app.
- Widget settings that appear in the editor panel with sensible defaults.
- Handling for Wix events and webhooks when the feature depends on them.
- A test on a development site covering fresh installs and updates from the previous version.
- A summary of what changed, plus release notes written for site owners.
- Checks on the phone view when the feature touches a widget.

## How we handle the work

We read your repository first, so the new code fits what is there. Then we send a short written scope with the changes we will make. Once you approve it, we build on a development site, test, and deliver the change in your repository.

The Basic package covers one feature or a few small fixes. Standard covers up to three features, new dashboard pages, new data fields and an updated widget panel. Premium handles a larger set, including backend endpoints, event handling and release notes. We can work on apps another developer built, as long as the code can be read and run.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe each feature as what the site owner will be able to do.
- Send reproduction steps for any bug.
- Tell us which owners or plans depend on the current behavior.
- Keep a copy of the current version before the work starts.

**Avoid:**
- Bundling unrelated changes into one vague request.
- Removing settings that owners already use.
- Skipping the update test, which is where most surprises appear.
- Changing the Dev Center configuration while we work on the code.

## Who this is for

An app owner whose original developer is no longer available. A product owner with a backlog of small requests from users. A team that needs extra hands for one feature without hiring.

## What we need from you

Repository access and collaborator access to your Dev Center, given by invitation so you stay in control. We never need your password. Please send the feature description, any screenshots or sketches, and the steps to reproduce bugs. A development site you already use is helpful, but we can create one.
